name: Safety Framework
summary: The lab publishes a framework with dangerous-capability thresholds, the safeguards that each threshold requires, and outside review.
description: A framework sets the rules before the pressure of a release. Thresholds and required safeguards make the lab's promises specific, so that others can check them.

criteria.label: Thresholds
criteria.description: Defined dangerous-capability thresholds, with the evaluations that detect them.

criteria.label: Required Safeguards
criteria.description: Safeguards that each threshold requires before training or release continues.

criteria.label: Loss of Control
criteria.description: It covers misalignment and loss of control, not only misuse.

criteria.label: Change Log
criteria.description: Each change is published with its reasons.

orgs.summary: OpenAI's Preparedness Framework has High and Critical thresholds and is filed as its SB 53 framework; outside review is optional, and requirements can change if competitors release.

events.title: Publishes beta Preparedness Framework with risk thresholds
events.summary: Sets risk levels for tracked categories and says only models at Medium or below after mitigation can be deployed. Says independent third parties will audit scorecard evaluations.

quote.text: Scorecard evaluations (and corresponding mitigations) will be audited by qualified, independent third-parties to ensure accurate reporting of results

sources.title: Preparedness Framework (Beta)

events.title: Signs Seoul frontier AI safety commitments
events.summary: Signs the Seoul commitments, which say signatories will publish a safety framework with thresholds and mitigations, and update it.

quote.text: publishing a safety framework focused on severe risks by the upcoming AI Summit in France

sources.title: Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Seoul Summit 2024

events.title: Publishes version 2 with safeguards reports and change log
events.summary: Adds AI self-improvement as a tracked category, safeguards reports and a change log. Third-party evaluation happens when OpenAI deems it warranted. Requirements may change if a competitor releases without comparable safeguards.

quote.text: If another frontier AI developer releases a high-risk system without comparable safeguards, we may adjust our requirements.

sources.title: Our updated Preparedness Framework
Preparedness Framework, Version 2

events.title: Publishes Frontier Governance Framework under California law
events.summary: Says the Frontier Governance Framework is its framework under California's TFAIA. Material updates go in a changelog with reasons within 30 days. External expert input is optional.

quote.text: Under California’s Transparency in Frontier AI Act (TFAIA), this FGF is our Frontier AI Framework

sources.title: OpenAI's Frontier Governance Framework
OpenAI Frontier Governance Framework
SB-53 Artificial intelligence models: large developers

events.title: Pauses RL training over critical cyber risk
events.summary: Says it paused reinforcement learning training for two weeks and holds its largest run after a model may have met the Critical cybersecurity threshold. Says it will evolve the Preparedness Framework.

quote.text: This included a two-week pause in reinforcement learning (RL) training on our latest models intended for deployment while we further hardened and red-teamed our research environments and expanded the coverage of our monitoring systems.

sources.title: Pacing model development in an era of cyber-critical capabilities

thresholds.commitment: High and Critical thresholds with capability evaluations.
thresholds.missing: OpenAI makes the threshold calls; no outside party publicly checks them.

required-safeguards.commitment: Safeguards must sufficiently minimize risk, as its Safety Advisory Group judges.
required-safeguards.missing: Requirements may change if a competitor releases without comparable safeguards.

loss-of-control.commitment: Tracks AI self-improvement; studies long-range autonomy, sandbagging and autonomous replication.
loss-of-control.missing: No outside party publicly checks these assessments.

change-log.commitment: Material updates with reasons in a public changelog within 30 days.

orgs.summary: Anthropic's RSP v3 has thresholds and Risk Reports that METR and SecureBio review in public; safeguards are public goals, and pauses depend on competitors.

events.title: Publishes Responsible Scaling Policy with AI Safety Levels
events.summary: Defines AI Safety Levels with capability thresholds and the security and deployment safeguards each level requires. Board approval is required for changes.

quote.text: Anthropic’s RSP has been formally approved by its board and changes must be approved by the board following consultations with the Long Term Benefit Trust.

Responsible Scaling Policy, Version 1.0

events.title: Updates policy with annual third-party procedural review
events.summary: Version 2.0 adds capability and safeguard reports, a public change log, and an annual third-party review of procedural compliance. Lists a condition for lower safeguards if other labs move ahead.

quote.text: On approximately an annual basis, we will commission a third-party review that assesses whether we adhered to this policy’s main procedural commitments

sources.title: Our updated Responsible Scaling Policy

events.title: Outside reviewer publishes sabotage risk report review
events.summary: METR published its review of the Summer 2025 pilot Sabotage Risk Report. It agreed that sabotage risk from Claude Opus 4 and 4.1 is low, but found some conclusions overconfident.

sources.title: Review of the Anthropic Summer 2025 Pilot Sabotage Risk Report

events.title: Publishes compliance framework for California SB 53
events.summary: Publishes a Frontier Compliance Framework to meet SB 53, which requires large frontier developers to publish and follow a catastrophic-risk framework.

quote.text: One of the law’s key requirements is that frontier AI developers publish a framework describing how they assess and manage catastrophic risks.

sources.title: Our compliance framework for California's SB 53
SB-53 Artificial intelligence models: large developers

events.title: Rewrites policy as version 3 with public goals
events.summary: Version 3.0 replaces hard safeguard commitments with public goals and Risk Reports, and adds misalignment thresholds. Says it will delay only if competitors also have strong safeguards.

quote.text: Rather than being hard commitments, these are public goals that we will openly grade our progress towards.

sources.title: Responsible Scaling Policy Version 3.0
Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy

events.title: Outside reviewer checks misalignment risk report
events.summary: METR reviewed the unredacted Sabotage Risk Report for Claude Opus 4.6. It agreed risk is very low but not negligible, and said evaluation awareness may weaken the alignment assessment.

sources.title: Review of the Anthropic Sabotage Risk Report: Claude Opus 4.6

events.title: Outside reviewer checks automated R&D threshold case
events.summary: METR reviewed the automated R&D section of the February 2026 Risk Report. It agreed risk is very low, but said the report's evidence, mainly a staff survey, is inadequate to establish this.

sources.title: Review of the "Risks from automated R&D" section in the Anthropic Risk Report (February 2026)

events.title: Outside reviewer checks bio risk and classifiers
events.summary: SecureBio reviewed the unredacted chemical and biological sections and the refusal classifiers. It agreed with the risk levels, but expert jailbreakers can still get around the classifiers. Anthropic had a veto right and did not use it.

sources.title: Review of Anthropic's Unredacted Chemical and Biological Risk Report: Claude Opus 4.6
Review of Anthropic's Chemical and Biological Risk Report: Claude Opus 4.6 (PDF)

events.title: Outside review questions automated R&D threshold call
events.summary: METR reviewed the August 2026 Risk Report with private data. It agreed catastrophic risk was low, but said an early-warning threshold was plausibly crossed and the public report understated acceleration.

sources.title: Review of the "Risks from automated R&D" section in Anthropic's Risk Report (August 2026)

events.summary: Version 3.1 joins misalignment with ML R&D into one domain with mitigation and risk acceptance steps, and adds tracked capability levels. Version 3.0 had added harmful manipulation.

events.title: Publishes Frontier AI Framework with stop threshold
events.summary: Sets high and critical risk thresholds for cybersecurity and chemical and biological risks. Says it will stop development at the critical threshold if risk cannot be mitigated.

quote.text: If a frontier AI is assessed to have reached the critical risk threshold and cannot be mitigated, we will stop development and implement the measures outlined in Table 1.

sources.title: Frontier AI Framework

events.title: Replaces stop rule with develop-with-mitigations
events.summary: Version 2 adds loss of control as a risk area and a change log, but the critical tier now permits development with mitigations instead of a stop. Version 2.1 renamed it the Superintelligence Scaling Framework.

quote.text: Critical threshold changed from "Stop" to "Develop with Mitigations."

sources.title: Advanced AI Scaling Framework, Version 2

events.title: Publishes high-level framework for open-weight releases
events.summary: Sets a staged path from API access to open weights, with internal and outside testing, including Apollo Research on loss of control. Says a detailed framework with stop conditions will follow.
